summary: The claim is biologically acceptable within its stated scope as apparent central-body mask width. The U-Net-primary comparative path preserves unusual morphology as measurable variation, does not use WT morphology as an acceptance or tuning target, retains single-slice and smooth long objects, and restricts technical invalidation to objective failures such as absent geometry or supported multi-object connectivity. Reporting uses specimen-level descriptive outcomes, labels the width as apparent, and does not claim molecular diameter, whole-organ volume, or a genotype effect.

findings.title: Width remains an apparent segmentation-derived phenotype
findings.impact: The implementation supports relative apparent-width description but cannot independently establish chromatin diameter or prove that a width difference is biological rather than boundary, focus, annotation, or PSF variation.
evidence: audits/claims_registry.json lists segmentation boundary, focus, annotation thickness, and lateral PSF as known limitations for MEAS-BODY-WIDTH-001.
V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:105-119 describes the contour-chord measurement and comparison with an area/length estimate, not external biological ground truth.
findings.recommendation: Retain the terms apparent body width and mask width in all biological outputs. Require manual-mask agreement across representative morphologies and independent specimens before making accuracy or genotype-effect claims.

limitations: No full image stack was run, as required; review relied on commit-bound RC6 evidence, source inspection, focused synthetic tests, and retained report artifacts.
The managed read-only environment had no writable temporary directory. A focused command still completed 36 tests, but temporary-file and Torch-cache-dependent tests could not be rerun locally.
Synthetic masks establish behavior for short, long, wide, thin, curved, low-ratio, and fused-looking cases but do not constitute external biological validation.
The retained study evidence contains one independent specimen per group, so no genotype inference is biologically supported.
No independent manual-mask dataset or optical PSF/deconvolution validation establishes true physical chromatin width.
recommended_follow_up: Before claiming biological accuracy, compare apparent body width against blinded manual masks across short, long, wide, thin, curved, fragmented-looking, and fused-looking nuclei.
Use multiple independent WT and mutant specimens for any group conclusion, with the specimen as the inferential unit.
Continue reporting width availability and missingness by specimen so insufficient chord sampling cannot differentially hide a phenotype.
Keep whole-organ volume and molecular-scale diameter outside this claim unless slice-specific organ masks and external optical validation are added.
